issue.title: [Task Manager] old idle task not run when there's a large backlog of idle tasks

labels.name: Team:ResponseOps
labels.description: Platform ResponseOps team (formerly the Cases and Alerting teams) t//

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
7.10.0-snapshot on staging cloud (post 7.10 FF)

I've been running some load testing on staging cloud with 7.10, and managed to get to a point where I have 96K tasks queued (for action execution), which appear to not being picked up to run.  While this is going on, alerts are running, so tasks are running, it's just that these old tasks are not running.

<details>
<summary>Here's an example task which is not being run, but should, as it's almost 12 hours old at this point:</summary>

```json
{
    "task": {
      "taskType": "actions:.server-log",
      "params": "{\"spaceId\":\"default\",\"actionTaskParamsId\":\"531c8827-191e-4fc9-bc09-3b25692e1ad2\"}",
      "state": "{}",
      "scope": [
        "actions"
      ],
      "attempts": 0,
      "scheduledAt": "2020-10-13T06:36:41.316Z",
      "startedAt": null,
      "retryAt": null,
      "runAt": "2020-10-13T06:36:41.316Z",
      "status": "idle"
    },
    "type": "task",
    "references": [],
    "migrationVersion": {
      "task": "7.6.0"
    },
    "updated_at": "2020-10-13T06:36:41.316Z"
  }
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Here's a task doc for a currently running alert</summary>

```json
{
    "migrationVersion": {
      "task": "7.6.0"
    },
    "task": {
      "taskType": "alerting:.index-threshold",
      "retryAt": "2020-10-13T15:40:45.196Z",
      "runAt": "2020-10-13T15:30:15.791Z",
      "scope": [
        "alerting"
      ],
      "startedAt": "2020-10-13T15:30:45.196Z",
      "state": "{\"alertInstances\":{},\"previousStartedAt\":\"2020-10-13T15:30:14.791Z\"}",
      "params": "{\"alertId\":\"4e8bbf2d-c7e7-4112-b1a8-d0bad05d9057\",\"spaceId\":\"default\"}",
      "ownerId": "kibana:a3dc9451-e65d-4245-89a2-442bab284249",
      "scheduledAt": "2020-10-13T05:22:58.374Z",
      "attempts": 1,
      "status": "running"
    },
    "references": [],
    "updated_at": "2020-10-13T15:30:45.246Z",
    "type": "task"
  }
```

</details>

Not exactly sure what I did to get in this state, exactly, but here are some of the things I was playing with.

1. create a cloud deployment, set env var `KBN_URLBASE` and `ES_URL` as appropriate for the following scripts
2. install https://github.com/pmuellr/es-apm-sys-sim , set `ES_URL` as appropriate 
3. run `ALERTS=100 whole-lotta-alerts.sh`, where that script is from [this gist](https://gist.github.com/pmuellr/f30331660ae032a0a7ccf2767aea3900)
4. run `es-apm-sys-sim 1 4 -k` - that allows you to change the cpu threshold with keystrokes; bump them all to 100% by holding down keys `1`, then `2`, etc
5. You'll now have 100 alerts firing every second (in theory) scheduling 4 actions every time the alert runs

Things will back up fairly quickly.  You can get the number of tasks queued (basically actions queued to run) via

```sh
curl $ES_URL/_cat/indices/.kibana_task_manager?v
```

You can kill `es-apm-sys-sim` so that the alerts will stop firing, and see if the actions will eventually get run, and then deleted from the tm index.  You can also easily "upgrade" Kibana, from say 1 1GB RAM instance to 4 8GB RAM instances, and that has worked at times to get the queued actions resolved.

To get to this state, I let ~100K tasks get queued, then killed `es-apm-sys-sim`, so that actions should STOP being queued, and hopefully resolved.  No more tasks got queued (as expected), but these old ones also never got run and so the tm index was left with ~100K action tasks.  Left it running overnight with 1 1GB Kibana instance, and they never got run.

issue.title: [DOCS] Fix the default value of scroll_size for update-by-query and d…

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Closes #63637.
The  default value of `scroll_size` in `update-by-query` and `delete-by-query` API is 1000 actually, but the value is 100 in the document.

issue.title: [Docs] Correct default scroll_size for update by query

labels.name: :Distributed/CRUD
labels.description: A catch all label for issues around indexing, updating and getting a doc by id. Not search.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The current [_update_by_query documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/docs-update-by-query.html#docs-update-by-query-api-query-params) mentions a `scroll_size` default of 100 and later another default of 1000.
I believe we use the default of 1000 defined in [AbstractBulkByScrollRequest here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/reindex/AbstractBulkByScrollRequest.java#L47) and changed the documentation
accordingly. 
This should also be used by "_delete_by_query" and the change in the common parameter doc should also reflect that already.

Closes #63637
